newsitem.title: USA: Intraday CSCE world sugar firms, breaks resistance.
newsitem.headline: Intraday CSCE world sugar firms, breaks resistance.

text.p: CSCE world sugar futures climbed higher amid mostly speculative buying, which sent benchmark July through several key levels and to a two-week high by midsession, dealers said.

July pierced nearby resistance at 10.92 cents, triggering buy stops which lifted the contract through key psychological 11.00 cents to 11.08 cents, its highest level since reaching 11.09 cents on April 30.
Profit-taking by the trade in the July/October and July/March spreads was also said to have given the market an early boost.
By midsession, July had eased back below 11.00 cents as producer selling emerged.
At 1130 EDT, July was 0.11 cent firmer at 10.99 cents per lb, having ranged from 11.08 to 10.89 cents. The rest of the board was trading 0.12 to 0.05 cent higher.
Volume was estimated at 16,819 lots as of 1100 EDT.
Open interest in July rose 1,057 lots to 74,636 lots, as of early Friday.

In fundamental news, the U.S. Department of Agriculture approved a 200,000 tonne increase in the U.S. sugar import quota, and forecast a 1996/97 sugar stocks-to-use ratio of 15.4 percent. The ratio is a key figure in setting the import quota.

The USDA allocated 1.7 million tonnes of sugar imports at the beginning of fiscal 1997, but said adjustments would be considered during the year. A ratio of 15.5 percent or less boosts the quota by 200,000 tonnes.
